<!-- pr-reviewer: 85baabe7bf8fa6b5736f2eb9f500e914c3d5b03d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks @mkinney for the thorough PathPilot work. I trial-merged with current main (9bb8d26) with no conflicts, built, and ran the touched suites and clippy.

### What looks good
- The inch path is right: every length is divided by 25.4 at four decimals, every feed by 25.4, rpm and angles are not scaled, and `G20` goes with `G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80` in the header. The same stream posted for an inch and a metric machine gives the same blocks, checked by `an_inch_machine_posts_every_length_and_feed_in_inches`.
- Dwell is posted in seconds, the same convention the Fanuc post uses for its `P` (`Math.round(p.P*1000)` there).
- Tool changes lift Z before `G30`, and the first move after a change positions X and Y before Z comes down. Tool numbers outside 1-1000 are refused by name, and the cutter-compensation and RTCP refusals are named.
- The machine file's `units` field is additive and skipped when unset, so no existing project file or post changes.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` is added in source.

### Local results (trial merge with main, plus the test-build fix)
- Test-build fix: the main test build failed on `drilling_cross_holder.rs` (`missing field coolant`). I cherry-picked the local commit 99c3072 (the fix branch is not on origin) and it is not counted against this PR.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app` tormach_post | 10 passed, 0 failed |
| conformance | 6 passed, 0 failed |
| machine | 32 passed, 0 failed |
| posting | 17 passed, 0 failed |
| fanuc_post | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| control_comp | 4 passed, 0 failed |
| arc_planes | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| vertical_arc_entry | 3 passed, 0 failed |
| scripting | 17 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-post` (all) | all passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Feed rounding in inch mode: `ff()` in `assets/posts/tormach.cps` writes ipm at two decimals (`(v/25.4).toFixed(2)`). At 10 mm/min that is 0.39 ipm against 0.3937, about 0.8% off, and below about 1 ipm the error grows. Three or four decimals would keep slow feeds accurate. Also, a positive feed under about 0.13 mm/min rounds to `F0`. Neither is reachable in practice, but a `F0` line would be a silent wrong feed, so a guard (refuse or clamp to 0.01 ipm) would be safer.
2. Machine values (travel, belt ranges, 250 ipm on Z) come from the PathPilot manual and cannot be checked from here. The maintainer may want the manual page references kept with the `.mch` file.
3. The reversal of G64 P0.025 and the `G53 G0 Z0` before G30 are contributor decisions that match PathPilot's own programs as described. A RECOMMENDED.md entry for them would fit the ledger process.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
